summary.name: Charcoal Drawing / Pastel is a supplemental Drawing and Illustration reference, not a named source-collection style. Charcoal and pastel are separate dry-media techniques, so one should be chosen as the primary medium for each project.
summary.visualIdentity: Dry-media drawing with visible paper tooth. Charcoal builds tonal mass, hatching and smudges; pastel layers soft pigment with visible grain. Powder edges stay localized, and marks are revealed or erased locally rather than covered by uniform noise.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: charcoal or pastel works best alone for tonal drawings, and hybrids help when figure motion or atmospheric depth is needed. Inferred: moody storytelling, documentary intros and illustrated explanations suit its tonal character. Listed patterns support both video and interactive HTML delivery; fit is not measured.
summary.limitations: Source review samples one frame per second from 1–8 seconds only. No motion, sub-second timing, audio or later scenes were verified, and no strong palette match was found. Two-color contrast checks do not prove readability over textures or video. Aspect ratio, duration and resolution are unspecified.
summary.palette: Background is scene-dependent. #EDE7DC and #353330 are authored example suggestions, not approved exact colors, so the background should be chosen from the scene. Their 10.233:1 contrast meets normal text. Gradients are disabled; tone comes from hatching, not added hues. Pastel colors must come from a pastel reference, and task-supplied exact colors override these examples.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Video uses composition time with smooth authored movement, while sharp cuts, impacts and reading holds remain available where the action calls for them. Grain stays fixed per frame rather than re-randomized. Interactive delivery can use chaptered or step-based scroll with a reduced-motion fallback. Motion-012 and motion-015 are optional and used only when scene-compatible; neither is required.
summary.audio: Audio is unspecified by the style, and no audio layer is mandatory. Suggestions to screen include restrained music or ambience, a voiceover if explanation is needed, and silence or sparse accents at reading holds. Sung vocals risk competing with narration. Any user audio choice takes priority, and no assets should be invented.
summary.assetRequirements: Rotoscoped figure motion requires supplied footage, and none is assumed. Local fonts, paper or grain layers, and brush assets must load before rendering. Procedural textures are an implementation choice, not a given. The source lists no reference images, palette samples or sources.
summary.combinations: style-090 provides rotoscoped motion for figure animation; it requires a charcoal palette only, fixed grain per frame, supplied footage, and avoidance of photo detail. style-101 provides atmospheric depth planes; grain stays anchored to paper, movement is limited, and no colors are added. Charcoal alone works best for tonal drawings.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for scene assembly, seekable timing, audio sync and export. Canvas 2D renders brushes, grain and smudge masks, while Pillow and Python prepare textures and masks. GSAP drives a paused timeline; @remotion/noise offers seeded grain, and chroma-js checks contrast. Remotion is fallback only, with a recorded reason. Verify forward, backward and direct seeks plus decoded frames.
